title: How MrBeast Cracked the YouTube Algorithm
the_thought: He made the click, then he made them stay.
hook:
A giant bright poster leans on a paint table. No letters on it. Just a face, a prize, and a promise you can feel. That poster is the click. Behind the paint table sits a hungry machine. The machine feeds people pictures. If they click, then sit still, the machine feeds them more. If they click and walk away, the machine gets shy. MrBeast cracked that machine. Not with a secret password. With a painted click, then a reason to stay.

He made the click, then he made them stay.

How? How does a kid with a camera teach a hungry machine to love him? The easy story says he just got lucky. The easy story says he just threw money. Luck does not sit still for forty hours. Money does not paint the poster first. Watch the poster. Watch the hungry machine. Watch who stays in the room.

We cannot see inside MrBeast's head. We cannot open YouTube's locked homework. There is no secret diary in this video. We have YouTube's own blogs from 2012. We have a counting stunt from January 2017. We have a Rolling Stone cover from April 2022. We have Guinness, The Verge, the BBC, and YouTube's own later party for half a billion people. Those papers are loud enough.

So keep one picture. A hungry machine that eats two foods. First food is the click. Second food is sitting still. Most makers fed it junk clicks, then wondered why it spit them out. MrBeast fed it both on purpose. He painted the click picture before the cameras rolled. Then he built a real stunt so people did not stand up. That is the whole map. Eight steps. First the machine changes its diet. Then a study club hunts the diet. Then a count to one hundred thousand. Then a giant painted card. Then a reason to stay in the room. Then the stunts get bigger. Then he walks past a music house that already sat on the throne. Then half a billion names on a list. If you can retell those eight steps, you can retell the video. Stay on the poster. Stay on the stay.

levels.name: Hungry Machine
beats:
Picture YouTube in 2012 as a hungry machine in a dark hall. It used to love one snack. Clicks. A loud picture. A weird title. A person taps. Then the person leaves. The machine still clapped, because a tap was a tap. That diet made junk. Pretty bait. Empty rooms.

August 10, 2012. YouTube wrote the diet change in public. Eric Meyerson, who talked to creators for YouTube, said discovery would surface videos people actually watch, over videos they click and then abandon. He even joked about cheap bait pictures. The machine was tired of being tricked.

Why does that matter for MrBeast? Because he was already posting by then. Bloomberg later said he had been posting since he was twelve, without amassing much of an audience. A hungry machine that loves junk clicks does not care about a kid who is trying. A hungry machine that loves sitting still might.

March 2012 had already started the shift on related and recommended videos. Time watched, not just taps. May 23, 2012, YouTube said it again. If people click and do not stick around, the video will not be shown as often. October 12, 2012, search got the same homework. Rank by time watched. Less clicking. More watching. That is not a rumor from a forum. That is the company's own blog, twice in one year, plus search.

August 24, 2012, they even warned about custom pictures. A picture that lies makes people leave. Leaving hurts watch time. Hurt watch time means the machine hides you. So the new diet had a simple rule a five-year-old can hold. Do not just make a loud door. Make a room worth sitting in.

The world before MrBeast's boom was full of people who only painted the door. They won a tap. They lost the sit. The machine started starving those people on purpose. That is the market before. PewDiePie was already a giant in games. Music houses were already stacking songs. None of that made a teenager in a small room inevitable. The machine had changed. Most people had not noticed the two foods.

Here is the kid sentence. The algorithm is not a wizard. It is a hungry machine with a new menu. Click, then stay. Or get small.

MrBeast did not write that menu. YouTube did. His later trick was to cook both foods on purpose. Success is not takeover yet. In 2012 he was not the king. He was a kid feeding a machine that had just gotten picky. The later legend likes to skip this hall. Do not skip it. September 15, 2021. A YouTube engineer wrote the same lesson in public. Clicks were not enough. Watch time was added in 2012. When they added it, views dropped about 20 percent right away. The machine had been counting junk taps. He also said the system has no recipe book. It learns from about 80 billion little signals. Surveys try to catch valued watch time, not just leftover sitting. We still cannot see the private ranking. Insufficient on purpose. The public menu is still two foods. Without the diet change, a forty-hour count is just a weird dare. With the diet change, a forty-hour count is a feast.

Hold one more simple question. If watch time is the food, why do pictures still matter? Because the machine cannot feed you a room you never enter. The door still has to open. YouTube said it would still look at clicks, with engagement leading. So a maker who only sits, with a boring door, also starves. Two foods. Both. That is the riddle the study club will try to solve. The hungry machine is not secret. It posted the menu. The hard part is cooking.

levels.name: Study Club
beats:
Fall 2016. Jimmy Donaldson is eighteen. Bloomberg says he drops out of college to hunt one mystery. How does a video go viral on YouTube? His mom had wanted school. Later reporting from the News and Observer said the school he briefly joined was Pitt Community College, not the big nearby university people kept naming. The school confirmed he was enrolled in the 2016 fall semester. Then he left. The point is not the campus. The point is the bet. He bet the hungry machine could be studied like homework.

Bloomberg says he was convinced he was close to unlocking the black box of rules that picks what gets recommended. He and a handful of friends ran daily calls. They watched what blew up. They watched what died. That is the study club. Not a wizard cave. A night table, phones, and a pile of other people's videos.

He told Bloomberg a sentence a child can copy. I woke up, I studied YouTube, I studied videos, I studied filmmaking, I went to bed and that was my life. That is not a flex. That is a schedule. Wake. Study the machine. Study the pictures. Study how a shot is built. Sleep. Repeat.

Why does a schedule matter more than a magic trick? Because the title asked how he cracked the algorithm. A crack can sound like one lucky key. The study club is the opposite. It is grinding on the menu YouTube already posted. Click, then stay. So what would a video look like if you designed both on purpose?

Bloomberg also says his first check from YouTube arrived when he crossed about 10,000 subscribers. It was not a windfall. For the first years he filmed on a phone. The laptop crashed. So the bet was not a pile of cash. The bet was time. Time is the same food the machine now loved.

We should be fair. Lots of kids studied YouTube in 2016. Most of them did not take over. Studying is not takeover. The study club is the unusual bet, not the crown. The crown needs a first breakthrough that matches the diet.

What was he hunting on those calls? Not a password. Patterns. Which pictures got a tap. Which rooms kept people. Which titles told the truth. Which stunts felt like a dare a kid would actually watch. The strategy suggests they were reverse-engineering the two foods, not chatting about feelings. We cannot hear the calls. We can hear the life sentence. Study, study, study, bed.

The funny part is he still had almost no crowd. Bloomberg's line is blunt. Posting since he was twelve, without amassing much of an audience. So the hungry machine had not chosen him yet. The study club was a kid talking to a locked door. Then he picked a stunt so simple it sounds like a joke. Counting. Not a car. Not a mansion. Numbers out loud, for longer than a person should sit.

Why counting? Independent later wrote that it crystallized the approach. Win people with high-concept stunts that take huge effort. Bloomberg's telling is that he was sure this one would work. We cannot prove the sure feeling. We can prove the sit. Forty-plus hours of murmuring numbers. That is a body bet, not a theory. The study club had been watching other people. Now one of them would become the video.

Hold the contradiction. The machine said, make what people watch. The study club said, then we will watch the watchers. Neither sentence is a crown. The next chapter is the first time the hungry machine actually sits down with him. Until then, he is still a kid with a schedule and a small list of names.

levels.name: One Hundred Thousand
beats:
January 2017. He sits in a chair and counts toward one hundred thousand. Bloomberg says the stunt took forty-plus hours. HuffPost, writing that same month, said he sped parts so the finished video could stay under twenty-four hours, because the edit tool capped there. So the dare was even longer than the thing you could click. That is a weird kind of honesty. The room was bigger than the door.

Bloomberg dates the upload January 8, 2017. Some later pages say January 9. This cut will not pick a fight over a day. Call it January 2017. The video was a smash. Bloomberg called it a viral smash. HuffPost watched the view count climb into the millions within days. People sat with a person saying numbers. Why?

Because the hungry machine could smell the stay. A count is almost nothing as a plot. It is everything as a sit. You can leave. Most people would leave. The ones who stay are watching willpower. Bloomberg later said the success of the count taught a lesson. Show how hard you are working. Huge effort, on camera, as the show. Not a trick thumbnail with an empty room behind it.

Near the end he looks wrecked and asks what he is doing with his life. That line is in Bloomberg's telling. It is funny because the answer is on the wall. He is feeding the second food. Sitting still, on purpose, until the machine notices.

Is that the algorithm crack? It is the first loud yes. Not the last. Success is not takeover. A smash count does not make you the most subscribed name on earth. It teaches a rule. If the stunt is real, people stay. If people stay, the machine shares you. If the machine shares you, more people see the next door.

So what is the next door? A bigger sit. A stranger sit. Bloomberg listed the cousins. A rap video on a loop for ten hours. A day in a prison. An asylum. A deserted island. The pattern is not random chaos. The pattern is a body in a room, doing a dare you can understand in one second, then proving it for a long time.

Why would a five-year-old care about forty hours? Because forty hours is a mountain of sitting. Kids know sitting is hard. Adults pretend it is easy. The count made sitting into a spectacle. The hungry machine, which had asked for sitting since 2012, finally got a feast designed as sitting.

We should not pretend this was the only video that ever kept people. Games kept people. Songs kept people. The difference is the design. He did not stumble into a sit. He built a sit as the product. The study club's homework shows up as a chair and a mouth counting. That is a breakthrough you can draw. Empty room. One chair. One tired face. A number that keeps growing. No mansion yet. No mountain of cash yet. Just the second food, cooked until it was ridiculous.

Then the flywheel starts to tick. More people find the count. More people click the next dare. Each dare has to be true, or the stay breaks, and the machine hides him again. That threat is already in YouTube's 2012 warning. Lie with the door, lose the room. The count did not lie. It was painfully, boringly true. Truth can be a stunt. That is the strange lesson. The algorithm did not want a poem. It wanted a person who would not stand up.

levels.name: Click Picture
beats:
A sit with a boring door still starves. Remember the two foods. The machine cannot love a room it never enters. So MrBeast started painting the door as hard as he painted the dare.

October 2021. Business Insider asked him about pictures. He said three things decide a click. Topic. Title. Thumbnail. He said he did not care if they spent up to 10,000 dollars making a thumbnail. He wanted the best possible one. He also said the picture has to match the video. If the door tells the truth, people stay. If the door lies, watch time dies, and the hungry machine walks away.

April 19, 2022. Rolling Stone put him on a cover. By then the channel had about 94 million subscribers. The magazine said he lured them with brightly hued thumbnails that cost 10,000 dollars each, paired with titles aimed at the algorithm. That is not a fan blog. That is a cover story repeating the same expensive-door habit.

Here is the kid picture. Before the cameras roll, he paints a giant click card. A poster. A face. A prize you can feel. No tiny afterthought. The card is the first product. The stunt is the second. He made the click, then he made them stay. The order is the crack. June 24, 2022. A stage at VidCon. A discovery man from YouTube sat with MrBeast. The discovery man said a kid sentence. Replace the word algorithm with the word audience. MrBeast told the room he sketches the click pictures before the cameras roll. He would rather have the panic before the stunt. He also said he goes back and paints old doors again. That usually helps. He said make 100 videos and improve one thing each time. When he was small, he said those videos sucked. The study club was that sentence, years earlier, wearing a night table. Most people film, then slap a picture on at midnight. He treats the picture like a second movie.

Why spend about 10,000 dollars on a still image? Because a better door, on a true room, is not decoration. It is distribution. The machine shows people a grid of doors. If your door is dim, you never get the sit you already paid for. Rolling Stone's number is a cost, not a magic CTR. This cut will not invent a percent. The sourced fact is the spend, and the reason he gave Insider. Match the content. Then the stay can happen.

The click card is also a trap if you cheat. YouTube said that in 2012. A lying picture annoys people. Annoyed people leave. Leaving hides you. So the expensive card is not a loophole. It is homework. Paint a true dare. Then do the dare. Then the machine has both foods.

Watch how this is not a name-swap of a search box or a red button or a friend list. Those are other companies' objects. This object is a poster on an easel, painted for a grid of faces. YouTube's grid. His poster. The algorithm did not hand him a crown for being loud. It handed reach to doors that open into rooms people actually sit in. He just took that sentence more seriously than almost anyone.

Is 10,000 dollars the secret? No. Plenty of rich people can buy paint. The secret is the pair. Expensive true door. Expensive true room. Cheap liars still starve. Cheap honest people can grow, but slower. He chose expensive and true. That is a strategic bet, not a personality quiz.

By 2022 the study club is a company. Crew. Sets. A man who still puts his own face on the card, because Insider said the recognizable face is often the focus. The door is him. The room is him doing a giant dare. The hungry machine does not care that it is him, except that people already know the face, so the click gets easier. That is a brand moat starting to grow. Brand is not a vibe. Brand is a face you already trust to do the thing on the poster.

So the title's verb, cracked, is not a hacked password. It is a craftsman's loop. Paint. Dare. Sit. Repeat. He made the click, then he made them stay. Say it again, because the rest of the rise is that sentence with bigger paint.

levels.name: Stay In The Room
beats:
Now the stay, without the poster in the way. What does sitting still look like when the stunts get huge?

YouTube's 2012 blogs already killed two cheats. Making the video tiny to fake a high percent who finish. Making the video fat to fake more minutes. Neither cheat is the food. The food is a longer session on YouTube, and a video that actually holds people. Meyerson said shorter is not automatically better. Longer is not automatically better. The comedy sketch that drags is the warning. So MrBeast's later giant videos are a risk. A two-minute joke can sit better than a twenty-minute pile of cash, if the pile is boring.

The strategy suggests he treated the first seconds as a promise, then paid the promise in the room. Insider said the picture must describe the content. Rolling Stone's titles are dares you can say in one breath. Extreme hide-and-seek. A dangerous escape room. You know why you clicked. If the video then wanders, the stay breaks. So the room has to be the poster, walking.

At that same VidCon, he said the number he watches most is who stays, and where they stand up. Most views, he said, come from people who are not already subscribed. The discovery man said the same. So the machine is not a fan club. It is a crowd that has not met you yet. That is why the stay matters more than a secret password. That is harder than it sounds. A true giant set costs money. Money comes after the machine has already shared you. So the flywheel has an order. A true sit earns reach. Reach earns money. Money builds a truer, bigger sit. The bigger sit needs a brighter card, or the new door is too small for the new room. Paint. Dare. Sit. Cash. Bigger paint. That loop is the takeover engine. Not a list of products. A loop.

Competitors were not stupid. A gaming host can sit people for hours in a world they already love. A music house can sit people on a song they already hum. MrBeast sat people on a dare they had never seen, with a face they learned to trust. Different food, same hungry machine. Fair map. The gamer wins on friendship with a character. The music house wins on a catalog of songs. He wins on a poster that is true, then a room that is huger than last time.

Why couldn't they just copy the loop? They could copy a dare. They could copy a bright picture. Copying both, at this scale, with a face people already click, is the moat. Scale plus brand plus the habit of paying the promise. That is not forever. It is hard.

The stay also has a moral that is really just math. If you cheat the door, you train people to leave. Leaving trains the machine to hide you. So honesty is not a sermon here. Honesty is watch time. The 2012 blogs and the 2021 Insider interview are the same sentence in two outfits. Do not bait and switch. The algorithm punishes the switch because people punish the switch with their feet.

By now the count chair looks small. That is the point of a rise. The first breakthrough is tiny next to the later warehouse. But the warehouse is still the count chair, wearing a costume. A body in a room, proving a sentence you already read on the poster. He made the click, then he made them stay. The stay is the lock. The click is the key. Lose either, and the hungry machine goes back to sleep.

levels.name: Bigger And Bigger
beats:
Once the loop works, the dares have to grow, or the machine gets bored, and so do people. That is the ugly side of a flywheel. You cannot freeze.

October 25, 2019. He and Mark Rober kick off Team Trees. Arbor Day Foundation later said the campaign hit about 20 million dollars on December 19, 2019, to plant about 20 million trees. One dollar, one tree. YouTube's own later blog said the campaign raised over 25 million to plant more than 25 million trees. Those later totals grew. The first public finish line was about 20 million that December. This cut will not pretend one press release is the only number forever.

Why put trees in an algorithm video? Because a tree campaign is still a click card plus a stay. The poster is a planet-sized dare. Plant 20 million trees. The room is a real fundraiser you can check. People sat with a stunt that was also a pile of good. The hungry machine does not grade morals. It grades sitting. The trees happened to be both.

YouTube's June 2026 recap also names Team Seas, more than 30 million dollars to pull trash from water, and Team Water in 2025 with Mark Rober, about 40 million dollars for WaterAid, with creators from 115 countries. Those are later, bigger costumes of the same loop. A poster you can feel. A room that is true. A sit that is also a crowd.

The warehouse sets grow too. Rolling Stone walked through escape rooms built like games. Live goats. A hallway. Cars hunting clues. That is not a kid in a chair anymore. That is a factory of dares. Factory is the right word. The flywheel has hired hands. The face on the card is still the same black-hoodie man, so the door stays familiar while the room becomes a stadium.

This is the moment a rise can fake being a biography of stunts. Do not let it. Each bigger set is only interesting if you remember why it is bigger. More stay. More reach. More cash. More set. The algorithm is still the 2012 menu. He is still cooking both foods. The pots are just enormous.

Success is still not the final takeover. In 2019 he is huge, not first. The music house is still sitting on the all-channel throne. The gamer is still the individual king. Bigger is not past. Bigger is the flywheel getting loud enough to threaten those seats.

There is a threat inside the loop too. If every poster must be huger, you can paint yourself into a corner. People can get numb. Copycats can shout. A platform can change the menu again. Scandals can make the face on the card feel unsafe. This cut will not invent a courtroom as the engine. It will say the engine can break if the stay breaks. The stay breaks if the promise on the card stops feeling true.

So the trees, the water, the giant games, they are not a charity detour and not a product list. They are proof the loop can wear many costumes without changing the sentence. Paint a dare. Do the dare. Make them stay. Then paint a louder dare. That is how a counting chair becomes a planet-sized poster without changing the hungry machine's diet.

levels.name: Past The Music House
beats:
November 17, 2022. Guinness World Records says MrBeast takes the record for most subscribers for an individual male, about 112 million, passing PewDiePie, Felix Kjellberg, who had sat there for close to a decade. BBC had already reported the pass around November 16. Call it mid-November 2022. The individual throne moves.

Be fair to the gamer. He did not lose because he was foolish. He built a character people sat with for years. Games. Talk. A face in a dark room. That is a different sit. Guinness even notes PewDiePie had helped fight a music house years earlier, and MrBeast had helped that fight too, with billboards and a Super Bowl stunt spelled on shirts. Then the student walked past the teacher. PewDiePie had even said he thought this would happen. A decade is a long sit. Then the click-and-stay factory outgrew the talking desk.

That is still not the all-channel throne. T-Series, a music house in India, held that one. BBC and The Verge are clear. A catalog of songs and trailers can beat a person, because songs never sleep. That competitor is not a joke. It is a library. Libraries are strong.

June 2024. The Verge, dated June 2, says MrBeast posted that he had avenged PewDiePie by overtaking T-Series. BBC, dated June 3, says the music label was toppled on Sunday after five years at the top. He also posted a one-day spike of about 2 million new names. The Verge put him around 268 million on the tracker they cited. Exact live counts twitch. The event does not. A person with painted dares walked past a music warehouse.

Why could the music house not stop him? Because their food was songs. His food was a true poster plus a true sit, refreshed, at a scale songs do not copy. They did not get stupid. He pulled away on a different axis. Subscriber lists are a blunt scoreboard. They are not the whole of YouTube. They are the scoreboard this title cares about, because the public reads the list as the throne.

October 15, 2023, later roundups say he passed 200 million along the way. This cut treats that as a mile marker, not a separate magic. The war that matters is gamer, then music house. Individual, then everyone. Two seats. Two dates. Mid-November 2022. Early June 2024.

The flywheel is now visible from space. Each giant dare paints a brighter card. Each card feeds the hungry machine. Each stay prints more names on the list. The list itself becomes a click. People tap the king to see the king. That is a network effect sitting on top of the original diet. Dangerous, because it can hide a weak room for a while. The 2012 machine still punishes a weak room eventually. The strategy suggests he kept paying the promise so the list could not float on fumes.

So the takeover, at this chapter, is not a password. It is a person beating a personality, then beating a catalog, with a loop those two models were not built to run. Games can sit. Songs can sit. A new true stadium, every few weeks, with a face you already tap, is a third beast. The music house still has songs. He has the list. The hungry machine, for now, is still eating his two foods.

levels.name: Half A Billion
beats:
June 12, 2026. YouTube's own blog. Michelle Beaver, Top Creators Lead. Jimmy Donaldson, globally known as MrBeast, is the first individual creator to reach 500 million subscribers. The post also reminds you he became the most-subscribed individual in November 2022, then the most-subscribed channel in June 2024. YouTube even points at a Squid Game-in-real-life video as a defining dare, and at giant creator fights for a million dollars, including a live sequel in April 2026. Those are costumes. The body is still the loop.

Half a billion is a pile of names too big to read aloud as digits. Round it. Half a billion. A list so long it looks like a nation. The hungry machine that once hid junk clicks is now a loudspeaker on one navy-hoodie face.

Is that forever? No. The threats are real. The platform can change the menu again, the way it did in 2012. A new machine, on phones, can sit people without his poster. Copycats can shout. A production that feels cruel can break the trust that makes the click easy. A TV deal with a shopping giant can be a different cage. He later talked about some of those cages as poor fits. This cut will not turn a side deal into the engine. The engine is still paint, then stay.

We also cannot see the private dashboard. We cannot see every test picture. Insufficient on purpose. Motive is inferred from what he spent, what he said to Insider, what YouTube printed in 2012, and what the list did. This appears to have been a craftsman's answer to a public menu, not a stolen key.

So the title answer, in one kid sentence. YouTube told everyone the machine wanted a click, then a sit. MrBeast treated that sentence like law. He painted the click on a giant card. He built a room that was the card, walking. He made the click, then he made them stay. The count proved the sit. The 10,000 dollar pictures proved the door. The trees and the stadiums proved the loop could grow. The gamer's throne and the music house's throne proved it could pass the old kings. Half a billion is the machine agreeing, in public, for now.

If you remember one joke, remember two foods. If you remember one object, remember the painted card. If you remember one date, remember 2012, when the hungry machine posted the menu, and January 2017, when a tired kid fed it forty hours of numbers. The later billions of views are that meal, reheated, bigger.

He made the click, then he made them stay. That is how MrBeast cracked the YouTube algorithm. Not a hack. A diet. Cooked on purpose. Served again and again, until the list looked impossible.
A talking gamer sat on the individual throne for almost ten years, with a different kind of sit. That is a different takeover, facing a different camera. This cut stays on the painted card.
